subject: Term rebalancing & usage anchoring proposal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Hassan <amir@brightline.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai, legal+contracts@brightline.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Term rebalancing & usage anchoring proposal

Hi Amir — following our call this morning, attaching a short proposal for rebalancing Brightline's renewal so it aligns with your product roadmap and spend seasonality. High-level: a multi-year term with a front-loaded ramp that we anchor to a committed usage baseline, plus two flexibility options for procurement to consider.

Key points (see attached forecast & draft amendment):
- 36-month primary proposal: total committed units split 30% / 35% / 35% across Y1/Y2/Y3 to reflect launch and growth phases.
- Quarterly true-ups against actual consumption (credits applied at next invoice).
- Auto-renew with 60-day opt-out window at the end of year 3; option to convert to pay-as-you-go if growth stalls.
- Co-terming: we can roll Brightline Analytics and Brightline Health under a single co-term so you only manage one renewal and one true-up cadence.
- Financials: 12% blended discount on the 3yr commit; we can trade toward smaller year-1 commit + frontloaded credits if procurement prefers lower initial spend.

If procurement prefers a shorter commitment, we have an alternate two-year structure with a smaller discount and larger true-up flexibility (details below). Please review with your finance/procurement and let me know which direction feels better — I can get a clean amendment drafted once you signal preference.

Attachments: Brightline_commit_forecast_Q1-3.xlsx, Draft_Amendment_BRG-4831.docx

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai

From: Amir Hassan <amir@brightline.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai, legal+contracts@brightline.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Term rebalancing & usage anchoring proposal

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the thoroughness. A couple quick asks from our side after reviewing with finance and product: 

1) Our leadership is pushing for less lock-in up front. Can you run a 24-month variant with: 25% / 35% / 40% split (Y1/Y2/Y3 equivalent prorated across 2 years) — essentially a milder frontload?
2) Procurement wants quarterly billing and a maximum 90-day true-up (no annual reconciliation only).
3) Co-terming is OK, but legal needs to see a clean limited dev/test data residency clause called out in the amendment.

If you can send a concise two-option summary (our CFO likes side-by-side options) we can accelerate legal review. We're targeting an internal approval meeting next Thursday.

—Amir
CTO, Brightline Health
amir@brightline.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Pricing note & negotiation levers for BRG-4831

Stephanie/Karthik — quick internal note before we reply to Amir. Proposed playbook: present two clean options (A/B) and make the 36mo the anchor. Talk tracks and levers: 

Option A (anchor) — 36 months, 30/35/35 commit, 12% blended discount, co-terming across subsidiaries, quarterly true-ups. We keep tighter committed economics and give 60-day opt-out at term end.

Option B (compromise) — 24 months, 30/70 split (frontload smaller now, bigger in year 2) with an 8% discount, quarterly billing, 90-day true-up cap, and a one-time frontloaded credit equal to 10% of Y1 committed spend to reduce Y1 cash hit.

Concessions we can offer without pulling pricing materially: 1) limited play on frontloaded credit (10% cap), 2) flexible true-up cadence (quarterly + 90d payment window), 3) explicit data-residency clause for dev/test environments (we'll log and isolate training data).

Ask: Karthik — confirm the capacity profile (gpus/nodes) will support a 30% burst above committed in Q1 if they need spike headroom. Monica — please confirm CS can own onboarding milestones tied to the co-term so we can justify the credits.

I'll draft the two-option summary and shipping language for legal.

-Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Pricing note & negotiation levers for BRG-4831

Confirming capacity and ops notes: we can guarantee the following for Brightline under either option A or B: 
- Buffer: we can provision up to 30% additional burst capacity for the first two quarters of the contract (region: us-west) without changing SKU; sustained increases beyond that trigger true-up.
- Latency/SLO: same p95 targets irrespective of commit; SLA exceptions handled via dedicated routing policy for co-termed accounts.
- Data residency: dev/test environments can be isolated to their VPC with customer-managed keys; production logs remain in Redwood-managed infrastructure per our SOC2 controls (we'll add clarifying language).

Attaching capacity_profile_by_region.pdf for legal/ procurement. If legal needs specific wording I can draft a short addendum.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Hassan <amir@brightline.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai, legal+contracts@brightline.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Term rebalancing & usage anchoring proposal

Hi Amir — thanks for the fast turnaround and helpful feedback. Per your ask, attached is a two-option side-by-side summary and a slightly revised amendment draft that calls out dev/test residency and the 90-day quarterly true-up option. High-level summary: 

Option A (Anchor) — 36 months
- Commit split: 30% / 35% / 35% (Y1/Y2/Y3)
- Discount: 12% blended
- Billing: quarterly; quarterly true-ups applied to next invoice
- Co-terming: included; single renewal cadence for subsidiaries
- Opt-out: 60-day window at end of term

Option B (Compromise) — 24 months
- Commit split: 30% / 70% (prorated across 2 years)
- Discount: 8% blended
- Billing: quarterly; 90-day true-up cap
- One-time frontloaded credit: 10% of Y1 committed spend applied as account credit

Next steps we recommend: 1) Confirm preferred option by Tuesday EOD (Jan 18) so we can route to legal for a clean DocuSign packet; 2) If you pick Option B, confirm the list of entities to include in co-terming and purchase order numbers for procurement; 3) Sign the amendment when it shows up in DocuSign — we will hold capacity for Q1 onboarding after signature.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/BRG-4831-amendment
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/BRG-4831

Attachments: Brightline_commit_forecast_Q1-3.xlsx, Draft_Amendment_BRG-4831.docx, capacity_profile_by_region.pdf

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement/legal if helpful.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
